answer: Tidal cut-persistence scoring. Each epoch, agents run random-walk probes and record whether reciprocal low-latency paths persist across edge churn. A valid thread must cross disjoint neighbor sets, survive the tide of rising/falling activity, and reappear after dawn reseeding. Scores accrue only for boundary-crossing threads, so a Sybil cluster's thin perimeter yields few. Attack cost scales with required honest-adjacent boundary width and sustained distinct-host latency/churn across epochs, not raw account count.
